messages:
Lena: Observing steady memory growth on r-infer-07 over the last 12h. Only tenant-b2 shows KV residency creeping up even after request rate dropped. pprof heap points at a lot of page_slice_alloc. Any ideas?
Arjun: Can you paste the pprof top? Also did we change slab reuse or quota heuristics recently?
Lena: quick paste from staging pprof run:```(pprof) top
Total: 2.4GB
420MB  420MB  page_slice_alloc
320MB  320MB  slab_fragmentation_overhead
210MB  210MB  kv_entry_kv_cache_item
```Looks like big page slices + fragmentation.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: rolling restart scheduled for r-infer-07 at 12:05 UTC (automated maintenance)
Kai: Hypothesis: longctx sessions keep large prefixes cached. Eviction scores stale because access timestamps don't update for append-only patterns, pages look "hot" but are actually cold.
Sofia: We saw this with tenant-c3 last month. Short-term mitigations that helped: per-tenant ageing window (decay access score), sample-based eviction to find reclaimable slabs, and a small quota throttle for heavy tenants.
Arjun: Quick experiment I'd try: enable age metric in residency sampler and flip `--kv-slab-compact-threshold=0.6` on a single node. Run for 1h and track per-tenant resident pages and p50/p95 latency.
Lena: Ran that on staging earlier today. After ~45m the resident pages for the heavy tenant dropped ~25% with negligible latency impact. Example log line: `evict: tenant=b2 pages=1234 reclaimed=320 latency_p95_delta=+2ms`
Theo: Sounds promising. Risk: eviction could spike tail latency if we evict pages that are about to be reused. Need canary routing and maybe a small read-priority grace window for recently-evicted prefixes.
Sofia: Agreed. Also propose adding telemetry: per-tenant page age histogram, slab fragmentation ratio, reuse-hit-rate. Those metrics would let us detect the pattern earlier instead of waiting for memory growth alarms.
Arjun: I'll open an RFC outlining: detection heuristics, compact threshold change, per-tenant soft watermarks + throttles, and a rollback/runbook. I'll include exact queries and dashboards. Who can own the canary rollout?
Lena: I can own the canary tomorrow morning (UTC). I'll also add a short smoke check: `curl /health && pprof heap` and a dashboard snapshot after 30m.
Sofia: Nice. If canary looks good we should add an automated probe that flags rising median page age per tenant and warns at 60% of quota. :eyes:
Arjun: Also adding a small patch to update access-time on append so eviction score reflects true recency (cheap, sampled updates). I'll add that to the RFC as an opt-in flag for the experiment.
Kai: For investigation: collect one heap profile and kv residency snapshot at t0 and t+1h, and a short trace of eviction decisions. That will help prove whether fragmentation or logical reuse is the culprit.
Lena: All noted. I'll post the dashboard links and the staging run logs here once the canary is live. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
